podcast.title: Contemporary Powerpop
podcast.body: The All-American Rejects are listed as a contemporary band that is part of the Powerpop tradition. They represent the genre's ongoing relevance and its evolution, influencing artists in the current musical landscape. "Well we have Jimmy Eat World, OkGo, All American Rejects, Simple Plan, maybe Fallout Boy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Members Collaborated with Weezer
podcast.body: A couple of guys from All-American Rejects collaborated with Weezer on the album "Ratitude." "A couple of guys from all American rejects."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.title: Third Wave Emo Chart Success
podcast.body: The All-American Rejects were among the bands whose emo records achieved mainstream success during the third wave of emo (early 2000s), with their albums reaching the top 10 on charts. "Emo records from bands like...All American Rejects... all rocketed into the top 10 on the album charts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: External Collaborators and Multiple Producers for Ratitude
xref.body: For "Ratitude," Weezer brought in outside collaborators for the first time, including Jermaine Dupri, members of All-American Rejects, Lil Wayne, Dan Wilson from Semi-Sonic, and the guys from Sloan (though uncredited and parts recorded in 2003). The album also had four producers, including Dr. Luke and Jacknife Lee, plus Rivers Cuomo, totaling five. "For the first time outside collaborators were brought in, including Germain Dupree, a couple of guys from all American rejects, Lil Wayne, Dan Wilson from Semi-Sonic, and the guys from Sloan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
